title: Free-parameter evaluation, whole-family substitution and coefficient mates
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme, with all profinite parameters and its small pro-etale sites in compatible coefficient universes [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-size-convention]. Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], put $B=p_X^*\Lambda$ [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-point-pullback, sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients], and use internal modules, ordinary unbounded derived categories, K-injective direct images, and derived tensor-Hom [sk-def-sfb-module-objects, sk-def-sfb-derived-categories, sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull, sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom]. For a profinite set $P$ let $U_P=X[P]$, with projection $\rho_P$ [def-sfb-profinite-test-objects], and let $A_P=\Lambda[P]$ be the free internal module on $h_P(Q)=C(Q,P)$ [def-sfb-condensed-free-module-generators]. For $N\in D(\operatorname{Mod}_{\Lambda})$ put
$$F_{X,P}(N)=p_X^*R\mathcal Hom_{\Lambda}(A_P,N),\qquad L_{X,P}(N)=R\rho_{P*}p_{U_P}^*N.$$
Define $c_{X,P,N}:F_{X,P}(N)\to L_{X,P}(N)$ to be the $\rho_P^*\dashv R\rho_{P*}$ adjunct of pulled-back derived evaluation on the universal $P$-generator over $U_P$. Write $H_{X,P}(K)=R\mathcal Hom_B(B[h_{U_P}],K)$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Let $\beta_{X,P,N}:F_{X,P}(N)\to H_{X,P}(p_X^*N)$ be the transpose of pulled-back evaluation, and let $\gamma_{X,P,K}:H_{X,P}(K)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\rho_{P*}\rho_P^*K$ be the generator-normalized slice isomorphism [lem-sfb-profinite-free-slice-derived-hom]. Then the following identities hold without any invertibility assumption on $\beta$ or $c$.

(1) $c=\gamma\circ\beta$ under the pullback-composition comparison. For a module $N$ in degree zero its $H^0$ is the free-module exponential-law comparison, evaluating on the universal generator. The maps $c$ commute with maps of $N$, continuous maps of $P$, and pro-etale base change of $X$, with the parameter restriction and base-change arrows defined by the pullback adjunction units. These are equalities of derived morphisms and remain equalities under successive slice restrictions [def-pur-localized-ringed-site].

(2) On $V=X[Q]$ for any profinite $Q$, let $K,K'\in D(\operatorname{Mod}_{B|_V})$, let $u:K\to K'$ be any morphism, and let $a:V[P']\to V[P]$ be any $V$-map of relative parameter objects. Write $H(a,u)$ for precomposition by the free-module map on $a$ followed by postcomposition with $u$. Write $L(a,u)$ for the map $R\rho_{P*}\rho_P^*K\to R\rho_{P'*}\rho_{P'}^*K'$ obtained from the unit for $a^*\dashv Ra_*$ and from $u$, with the canonical composition comparisons. Then
$$\gamma_{V,P',K'}\circ H(a,u)=L(a,u)\circ\gamma_{V,P,K}.$$
In particular a continuous $\alpha:Q\times P'\to P$ defines such an $a$ by $(q,p')\mapsto(q,\alpha(q,p'))$, and the displayed identity is over all of $X[Q]$. Its evaluation formula is $f(q,p)\mapsto u(q)(f(q,\alpha(q,p')))$, interpreted on generalized parameter sections, not just on points. When the relevant $\beta$ are invertible, the corresponding action on $F$ is defined independently of $c$ by $\beta^{-1}H(a,u)\beta$, and the same square for $c$ follows. For finite free models $N=\Lambda^r$, $N'=\Lambda^s$, this action agrees with multiplication by the matrix of any $B|_V$-linear map between their pullbacks, including matrices whose sections do not come from the point; it is independent of the checking bases.

(3) For any morphism of commutative condensed rings $\varphi:\Lambda\to\Lambda'$ and any $n:N\to\operatorname{Res}_{\varphi}N'$ with $N'\in D(\operatorname{Mod}_{\Lambda'})$, the coefficient-comparison square for $c$ commutes after scalar restriction [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars, sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars]. Explicitly, write $a:F_{X,P}^{\Lambda}(N)\to\operatorname{Res}_{p_X^*\varphi}F_{X,P}^{\Lambda'}(N')$ for the comparison obtained by $n$ and the derived tensor-Hom adjunction, with free-generator scalar extension $[t]\mapsto[t]$, and $b:L_{X,P}^{\Lambda}(N)\to\operatorname{Res}_{p_X^*\varphi}L_{X,P}^{\Lambda'}(N')$ for the direct-image coefficient mate induced by $n$. Then
$$b\circ c^{\Lambda}_{X,P,N}=\operatorname{Res}(c^{\Lambda'}_{X,P,N'})\circ a.$$
Scalar extension here is derived K-flat tensor; no flatness of $\varphi$, exactness of scalar extension, or invertibility of $a,b$ is asserted. Whenever both $c$ maps are isomorphisms, their inverses satisfy the inverse square. No finite-subextension-valued coefficient replacement or completion occurs.

proof.text: Use the generator-preserving identification $p_X^*A_P=B[h_{U_P}]$ from [lem-sfb-profinite-free-slice-derived-hom]. Work in section-ring modules through [lem-sfb-module-object-ringed-site-derived-comparison] and [lem-sfb-internal-section-scalar-adjunction]; these preserve derived evaluation, tensors and scalar adjunctions, including on slices. The point inverse image and its composition maps are exact and monoidal by [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-point-pullback]. The derived tensor comparison is available for this geometric morphism by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. Thus the transpose defining $\beta$ is the actual pulled-back evaluation, with its specified tensor comparison. Use the derived pull-push adjunction of [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull] and the closed adjunction of [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom] throughout; neither requires $\beta$ to be invertible.

source.place: Tags 08J7/08J9, section-internal-hom and lemma-internal-hom; Tag 07A4, lemma-pullback-tensor-product; agent application to the point morphism

proof.text: Let $\iota_P:\mathbf1\to\rho_P^*B[h_{U_P}]$ be the universal generator. The normalization in [lem-sfb-profinite-free-slice-derived-hom] says that the $\rho_P$-transpose of $\gamma$ is evaluation after inserting $\iota_P$: on a test it sends a family of homomorphisms to its value on the tautological map to $U_P$. Consequently the transpose of $\gamma\beta$ is $\rho_P^*F_{X,P}(N)\xrightarrow{1\otimes\iota_P}\rho_P^*F_{X,P}(N)\otimes^L\rho_P^*B[h_{U_P}]\xrightarrow{\rho_P^*\mathrm{ev}(\beta\otimes1)}\rho_P^*p_X^*N$. By the definition of $\beta$, this is precisely the evaluation defining $c$. The adjunction Hom map is injective, so $c=\gamma\beta$; the final target identification is the pullback-composition comparison supplied by the same cited node.

source.place: Tag 08J7, equation-internal-hom; agent two-adjunction evaluation calculation

proof.text: For degree-zero $N$, the relevant ringed-site module categories are Grothendieck by [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaves-grothendieck], hence have enough injectives by [lem-sp-grothendieck-enough-injectives]. Choose nonnegative injective resolutions using [lem-weil-pbc-left-exact-injective-resolution-degree-zero]; these are K-injective by [lem-weil-pbc-bounded-below-injectives-kinjective]. The degree-zero kernel of the Hom complex is the ordinary internal Hom into $N$, and the analogous kernel for $\rho_{P*}$ is $\rho_{P*}p_{U_P}^*N$, by the left-exact functor clause of the same degree-zero lemma. Point inverse image preserves this kernel because it is exact. Apply the evaluation formula of step 2 to these kernels: on a test $T$ and generalized generator $t:T\to U_P$, a homomorphism $f$ is sent to $f([t])$. This is exactly the free-module exponential-law comparison; no invertibility or higher-degree vanishing is asserted.

source.place: Tag 08J7, K-injective Hom-complex construction and equation-internal-hom; agent degree-zero kernel calculation

proof.text: For a morphism $v:N\to N_1$, both proposed composites for $c$ have transpose $p_{U_P}^*v$ after universal-generator evaluation, by naturality of the closed adjunction. For a continuous $j:P'\to P$, the covariant free map sends $[t']$ to $[jt']$ by [def-sfb-condensed-free-module-generators]. The transpose of parameter restriction on direct images is restriction of the same evaluation along $X[j]:U_{P'}\to U_P$: the unit inserts that restriction and the counit evaluates it. Thus both parameter composites send the generalized generator $t'$ to evaluation at $jt'$. Injectivity of the two adjunction transposes gives both naturality squares as derived morphisms.

source.place: Tags 08J7 and 07A7, equation-internal-hom and remark-base-change; agent naturality calculation

proof.text: Let $g:Y\to X$ be a pro-etale base change and $g_P:Y[P]\to X[P]$. Identify the composite pullbacks by [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-point-pullback]. The base-change arrow for $R\rho_*$ is the mate of this pullback square [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]; its transpose is pullback of the counit. Hence the transposes of the two maps from $g^*F_{X,P}(N)$ to $R\rho_{Y,P*}p_{Y[P]}^*N$ are both the pullback along $g_P$ of the evaluation in step 2. The tautological generator pulls back to the tautological generator because the representable identifications in [lem-sfb-profinite-free-slice-derived-hom] preserve generators. Equality follows by the adjunction. Derived internal Hom restricts to slices compatibly with successive restrictions by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction], and [lem-sfb-module-object-ringed-site-derived-comparison] preserves that identification. For two restrictions the equality is therefore the restriction of this same evaluation equality, with the canonical composition maps. Their direct-image comparisons exist by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition], and [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] identifies the successive mates with the composite one.

source.place: Tags 07A7, 0E46, 0E47, 0D6E and 08JB; remark-base-change, the two compose-base-change remarks, lemma-derived-pushforward-composition and lemma-restriction-RHom-to-U

proof.text: Work over $V$, write $W=V[P]$, $W'=V[P']$, $C=B|_V$ and $D_W=C[h_W]$. For $a:W'\to W$, put $d_a:D_{W'}\to D_W$, with $[t']\mapsto[at']$. To compare the two sides of (2), transpose by $\rho_{P'}^*\dashv R\rho_{P'*}$. By the normalization of $\gamma$ their transposes are both $\rho_{P'}^*H_{V,P}(K)\to\rho_{P'}^*K\xrightarrow{\rho_{P'}^*u}\rho_{P'}^*K'$, where the first map evaluates at the generator $a\iota_{P'}$. On the right side this follows by inserting the unit for $a$ and contracting its counit: the triangle identity leaves restriction of evaluation along $a$. On the left it is the defining evaluation equation for precomposition by $d_a$ and postcomposition by $u$. Thus the transposes, and hence the original maps, agree. This applies to arbitrary derived $u$: the closed adjunction is natural in derived morphisms, rather than merely chain maps; alternatively [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] represents $u$ between K-injective models up to homotopy. Direct-image composition is [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition].

source.place: Tag 08J7, equation-internal-hom; Tags 07A7 and 0D6E; agent graph-evaluation transpose

proof.text: Take $V=X[Q]$ and $a(q,p')=(q,\alpha(q,p'))$. For every test $T\to V$, precomposition sends the generalized parameter $t':T\to V[P']$ to $at'$, so step 6 evaluates at $\alpha(q,t')$ and then applies the pullback of $u$. In degree-zero function notation this is $f(q,p)\mapsto u(q)(f(q,\alpha(q,p')))$. For general derived objects the formula denotes the evaluation transpose proved in step 6, not a claim that derived objects are sets of functions. Since $q,t'$ range over all generalized sections over all tests, this calculation is over the entire object $X[Q]$; it never tests equality only on ordinary points.

source.place: Tag 08J7, equation-internal-hom; agent specialization of step 6 to a profinite family

proof.text: Whenever the two $\beta$ maps are invertible, define $A=\beta_{\rm target}^{-1}H(a,u)\beta_{\rm source}$. Then $c_{\rm target}A=\gamma_{\rm target}H(a,u)\beta_{\rm source}=L(a,u)c_{\rm source}$ by steps 2 and 6. For finite free degree-zero models, write $u(e_j)=\sum_i m_{ij}e'_i$ over $V$. The entries are sections of $C$ on $V$, without any point-origin condition, by [lem-sfb-ringed-site-free-matrix-scalar-extension]. Evaluation is $C$-linear, so its composite with $u$ sends $(f_j)$ at $t'$ to $(\sum_j m_{ij}f_j(at'))_i$. The evaluation transpose therefore identifies the conjugated action with that matrix action. For new bases $eS,e'T$, the entries and vectors become $T^{-1}MS$ and $S^{-1}f$; the resulting vector is $T^{-1}Mf$, exactly the target coordinate change. Thus the action is independent of checking bases.

For (3), use $E=\Lambda'\otimes_\Lambda^L-$ and $r=\operatorname{Res}_\varphi$, and the corresponding $E_T,r_T$ on each scheme. The normalized scalar adjunction is [sk-def-sfb-derived-extension-of-scalars]; it is transported to section modules without flatness by [lem-sfb-internal-section-scalar-adjunction]. Its derived tensor comparison is [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] applied to the identity topos with structural ring map $\varphi$. For every geometric inverse image $h^*$ in use, [lem-sfb-kflat-scalar-comparison-normalization] supplies $E_{\rm source}h^*\cong h^*E_{\rm target}$, normalized by $x\mapsto1\otimes x$, compatibly with composition. This applies to the condensed-point morphism as well: its source is the small profinite site and its inverse image is exact by [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-point-pullback]. Thus $p_X^*r\cong r_Xp_X^*$ is the action identification, and the direct-image coefficient comparison is the mate of this scalar/pullback square. No preservation of K-injectives by $r$ is being used.

source.place: Tag 07A6, lemma-adjoint; Tag 07A4, lemma-pullback-tensor-product; Tag 0D6D and scalar-inverse-image normalization

proof.text: The free module $R[h_U]$ on any representable in either site is the sheafification of $T\mapsto\bigoplus_{t:T\to U}R(T)$: maps out of that presheaf, and then out of its sheafification, are precisely maps from $h_U$ into the underlying module sheaf. It is therefore the extension-by-zero object in [lem-pc-sites-modules-j-shriek-flat], hence flat. Concentrated in degree zero it is K-flat directly from [def-pc-kflat-complex]: tensoring an acyclic complex by an exact tensor functor preserves its zero cohomology. Extension of scalars is consequently computed without a resolution on this object. The ordinary scalar adjunction and the free adjunction now give $E(R[h_U])\cong R'[h_U]$: both represent maps from $h_U$ to the underlying $R'$-module. The unit sends $[t]$ to $[t]$, so this is the generator-preserving identification. Apply this both to $A_P$ on the profinite site and to $B[h_{U_P}]$ over $X$.

source.place: sites-modules.tex Tag 03EV, lemma-j-shriek-flat; sites-cohomology.tex Tag 07A6, lemma-adjoint; agent free-adjunction identification

proof.text: Let $n^\sharp:EN\to N'$ be the scalar adjunct of $n$. The scalar-Hom comparison $e:R\mathcal Hom_\Lambda(A_P,N)\to rR\mathcal Hom_{\Lambda'}(A'_P,N')$ is uniquely characterized by tensor-Hom and scalar adjunction: its twice-transposed map is $E(R\mathcal Hom_\Lambda(A_P,N))\otimes^L A'_P\cong E(R\mathcal Hom_\Lambda(A_P,N)\otimes^L A_P)\xrightarrow{E(\mathrm{ev})}EN\xrightarrow{n^\sharp}N'$. The tensor identification is step 9 and the free identification is step 10; existence and uniqueness of this transpose use [lem-sfb-closed-scalar-hom-comparison]. Pull this equation to $U_P$, insert its universal generator, and use the normalized scalar/pullback comparison from step 9. The generator remains $[t]$, so the resulting equation is $\operatorname{Res}(\widetilde c')\circ\rho_P^*a=\widetilde n_U\circ\widetilde c$, where $\widetilde c,\widetilde c'$ are the geometric transposes of $c,c'$ and $\widetilde n_U:p_U^*N\to r_Up_U^*N'$ is induced by $n$. This is an equality of derived maps by injectivity of the scalar and closed Hom bijections, not an elementwise test on cohomology.

source.place: Tags 07A6 and 08J9, lemma-adjoint and lemma-internal-hom; agent scalar and closed transpose of evaluation

proof.text: Define $b$ by first applying $R\rho_{P*}$ to $\widetilde n_U$ and then the direct-image coefficient mate of step 9. By the mate equation [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate], the geometric transpose of $b\circ c$ is $\widetilde n_U\circ\widetilde c$. The transpose of $r_X(c')\circ a$ is $r_U(\widetilde c')\circ\rho_P^*a$, using the same action identification. These are equal by step 11; hence $b\circ c=r_X(c')\circ a$. The canonical pullback-composition comparisons identify $\rho_P^*p_X^*$ with $p_{U_P}^*$ by [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-point-pullback]. The equality remains valid for nonflat $\varphi$, because step 11 uses the derived adjunction rather than exact scalar extension. In particular no coefficient mate is assumed invertible.

source.place: Tag 07A7, remark-base-change; agent equality after the geometric adjunction transpose

proof.text: If both $c,c'$ are isomorphisms, multiply the equality of step 12 on the left by $r_X(c')^{-1}$ and on the right by $c^{-1}$. This gives $a\circ c^{-1}=r_X(c')^{-1}\circ b$, the inverse square. All constructions above take place in ordinary unbounded derived categories with the originally specified ring objects. No completion or change to finite-subextension-valued functions occurs.

Q39 splits a node that Q08 created today from old parent steps 6-8. Its statement and stmt_deps are identical to the Q08 copy. There is no repair note, no new node, no SGA citation and no cycle; the only citer is the parent. The 13 steps keep every argument of old steps 6-8 and write them out in more detail. Sources read: Stacks 08J7, 08J9 and 08JB (sites-cohomology l.8836-8934), with 08FI and 03EV mapped to their labels. Checks: (1) c=γβ by uniqueness of adjuncts, using only the free-generator normalisation of lem-sfb-profinite-free-slice-derived-hom. Degree zero uses a nonnegative injective resolution, the left-exact H^0 clause and exactness of p_X^*. Naturality in N and P and base change follow by transposes, mates and mate-pasting, with successive slices from the exact-restriction node. (2) Over V=X[Q] both ρ_{P'}-transposes are evaluation at [a] followed by u, so the square holds for arbitrary derived u. The graph of α is a V-map because X[Q][P]=X[Q×P]. The matrix clause holds because β is additive and B-linear and multiplication by a section of Γ(V,B) is natural on D(B|_V); the basis change T^{-1}MS is correct. (3) a=p_X^*e from the closed-scalar-Hom comparison, with μ coming from the derived tensor-pullback node for ring map φ. R[h_U]=j_{U!}O_U is flat, hence K-flat in degree 0, with [t]↦[t]. b is the conjugate of θ (kflat-normalization) after Rρ_*(ñ). Both transposes reduce to ev'(e⊗η)=n∘ev. This holds for nonflat φ, and no invertibility is assumed. Edge cases checked: empty P, point P, rank 0, empty X, Z→Z/2. No duplicate among point-pullback-derived-hom, ringed-slice-evaluation-transpose or derived-hom-substitution-coherence. The 13 off-unit tool uses are generic and accepted. Batch 5: the new citation lem-sfb-kflat-scalar-comparison-normalization reaches lem-pod-derived-exact-square-composition, which is a purely formal pasting lemma for exact functors between arbitrary abelian categories. It is neither Poincaré duality nor a step of its proof, so it is outside the assumptions and accepted.
